candidates.explanation: The end of this method was not visible, so this is inferred. AuthService.register spreads a DTO that has no `provider` field, so `create` must default the provider to `AuthProvidersEnum.email` when it builds the user. The stored user ends up with provider `google`, so `validateLogin` fails its `user.provider !== AuthProvidersEnum.email` check and returns `needLoginViaProvider:google`. The likely cause is a wrong fallback or hardcoded value in the `usersRepository.create({... provider: ...})` call.

Registration never sets `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` when it calls `usersService.create`. It relies on a default in `create`, and a wrong default there makes the user a non-email-provider user. The `...dto` spread could also carry through an unexpected provider value.
This check reports the `needLoginViaProvider` error from the stored `user.provider`. It is probably correct, and it exposes the wrong provider value saved at registration.

fix.description: In `UsersService.create`, default the provider to email with `provider: createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`. Also pass `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` explicitly in `AuthService.register`.

candidates.explanation: The end of this method was not visible, so this is inferred. AuthService.register spreads a DTO that has no `provider` field, so `create` must default the provider to `AuthProvidersEnum.email` when it builds the user. The stored user ends up with provider `google`, so `validateLogin` fails its `user.provider !== AuthProvidersEnum.email` check and returns `needLoginViaProvider:google`. The likely cause is a wrong fallback or hardcoded value in the `usersRepository.create({... provider: ...})` call.

Registration never sets `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` when it calls `usersService.create`. It relies on a default in `create`, and a wrong default there makes the user a non-email-provider user. The `...dto` spread could also carry through an unexpected provider value.
This check reports the `needLoginViaProvider` error from the stored `user.provider`. It is probably correct, and it exposes the wrong provider value saved at registration.

fix.description: In `UsersService.create`, default the provider to email with `provider: createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`. Also pass `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` explicitly in `AuthService.register`.
